summary: A brick light on a Penobscot Bay headland at Rockland Harbor, first lit in 1825; the current tower dates from 1852, and the American Lighthouse Foundation runs climbing tours.

lens.note: Fourth-order Fresnel installed 1856 (USLHS); still in the lantern (NRHP, USLHS).

structures.note: Current tower on a granite foundation (USLHS). ALF: 26 ft in one place, 30 ft in another. The first (1825-26) tower is described as brick in one NRHP passage and granite in another.
Dwelling built 1825 under the articles of agreement, 34 x 20 ft; ell, second story and piazza added about 1854 (NRHP). USLHS: keeper's quarters 1854.

access.note: Owner records say open to the public; climbing tours Memorial Day to Columbus Day (ALF).

visit.tours: Climbing tours Memorial Day to Columbus Day (ALF)
visit.note: Interpretive center in the first floor of the keeper's house (ALF).

facts.agency: American Lighthouse Foundation (licensee); US Coast Guard (owner, per ALF)

events.note: Articles of agreement dated 18 April 1825 for a lighthouse and dwelling for $1,888 (NRHP)
Keeper Isaac Stearns lit the light for the first time, September 1825 (NRHP)
Dwelling altered by an ell, a second story and a piazza, about 1854 (NRHP)
Schooner Hero smashed on the rocks at Owls Head in the equinoctial gale of 21 March 1847; sloop Louisa hit at Crockett's Point (NRHP)
Schooner Dove went ashore at Ash Point on 24 January 1850 and was a total loss (NRHP)
December 1850 gale: five vessels ashore between Owls Head and Spruce Head; a Haverhill schooner's three aboard survived after being iced in; account names Masters (NRHP, after Snow)
Keeper Llewellyn S. Norwood died at his home at Owl's Head, 13 April 1911 (Ellsworth American)
Illuminant changed from incandescent oil vapor to electric incandescent (Bulletin 1925)

keepers.name: Isaac Stearns
keepers.note: First keeper. Lit the light for the first time in September 1825 (NRHP). Retired 1838.

keepers.name: William Masters
keepers.note: Resigned August 1849 in favor of Henry Achorn (NRHP). The NRHP also names Masters as keeper in December 1850.

keepers.name: Joseph G. Maddocks
keepers.note: The NRHP spells the name Haddocks, dates his arrival to 1873 and says he left in 1896. Wounded at Gettysburg, former shipbuilder, married Clara Emery of Owls Head (NRHP).

keepers.name: Llewellyn S. Norwood
keepers.note: Keeper 1895-1911. Died at his home at Owl's Head on 13 April 1911 of heart disease (Ellsworth American, 19 and 26 Apr 1911). The two notices disagree on years of service (twenty vs fifteen).

keepers.name: Augustus B. Hamor
keepers.note: Last regular keeper of the old Lighthouse Service here (NRHP). Entered the service in 1913; 17 years at Egg Rock first.

notes_for_editor: 1) NRHP narrative (sections on the 1847-1850 wrecks, the 1850 rescue, Haddocks/Maddocks, Hamor and the dog story) follows Edgar Rowe Snow's The Lighthouses of New England, as the nomination says. Snow is copyrighted; the story paraphrases and quotes only short phrases. Snow's book was not read directly. 2) NRHP says Masters resigned in 1849 but names him keeper in Dec 1850; flagged in the story. 3) Keeper name Haddocks (NRHP) vs Maddocks (roster); arrival 1873 (NRHP) vs 1872 (roster); departure 1896 (NRHP) vs 1895 (roster). Not resolved. 4) First tower: NRHP says brick in one passage and granite in another. Current tower: brick (USLHS, ALF). 5) ALF gives 26 ft and 30 ft for the tower height. 6) Owner: USLHS says American Lighthouse Foundation; ALF says the Coast Guard owns the light and licenses it to ALF. The story reports ALF's statement. 7) Norwood: Ellsworth 26 Apr says 'died April 13' and 'fifteen years' service'; Ellsworth 19 Apr says 'for the last twenty years' in the service. Roster 1895-1911. Story says 'died in office that April'. 8) The 1894 tests are on scan page 717 (the printed page is probably 308 but was not checked). 9) The 1850 gale's 'Haverhill schooner' was owned by Henry Butters per the NRHP. The name is not given. 10) The 1925 Bulletin entry gives no date for the illuminant change. Year is from the volume. 11) The NRHP's 'Light Tower built 1826' conflicts with 1825 first lighting (USLHS 1825, NRHP 1825). 12) Post-1960 keepers on the roster are listed only by name, with no personal details. 13) Owls Head ALF news items (2025 bicentennial, Norwood memorial stone 2025) were not read in full. 14) Fact-check 2026-10-22 (fixes): the 1893 test used the tender Myrtle's 6-inch whistle, not an 8-inch whistle (story corrected). 15) NRHP physical description calls the light tower brick and dates it 1826; USLHS and ALF date the present brick tower to 1852 (story states both). 16) NRHP physical description gives the 1826 dwelling as 34 x 21 ft, two stories with an attached shed; the significance section gives 34 x 20 ft, one story, with the second story added about 1854. Not reconciled; story uses the significance-section figures. 17) NRHP says Stearns was succeeded by Masters in 1838 and also that Masters 'became keeper' in 1845; roster has Penley Haines 1841-1845 (story states this). 18) Norwood: 19 Apr 1911 notice says 'for the last twenty years' in the service; 26 Apr headline says 'Fifteen Years' Service'; both give death 13 April. The 19 Apr notice says he died at his home, so 'died in office' is not used. 19) Roster spells the 1849 successor Achora; the NRHP's Achorn is used in the story with both spellings stated. 20) The OCR of the 26 Apr notice reads 'heirt disease' and the 19 Apr notice reads 'April IS'; read as heart disease and 13 April. 21) The 1850 gale account in the NRHP is extracted from Snow and is dramatic in places (dialogue, feelings); the story keeps only the sourced facts. 22) Printed page of the 1894 Owls Head tests not read; scan page 717 is cited. 23) The 1894 report's scan page 717 text was checked by reading the cached OCR; corpus.py page did not match 'Owl'.

fog_signal.note: 1894 report (fog-signal tests, Owls Head): regular 1,000-pound bell tested 7-8 Sept 1893 and 13-14 June 1894; a 960-pound bell and the tender Myrtle's 6-inch whistle tested 7-8 Sept 1893 (LHB 1894).
